To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) The merger of a binary black hole (BH) is a generic consequence of hierarchical galaxy merging, but the merger timescale is much too long for the binary lifetime to be comparable with the age of the universe.

(i) binary BH mergers can occur in a timescale of a few million years; (ii) this timescale can be shorter than the lifetime of the gas disk; (iii) the merger rate is proportional to the gas mass in the disk; (iv) the merger timescale is inversely proportional to the gas density; (v) the merger timescales is proportional to the BH binary orbital separation; (vi) the merger rate depends on the gas mass in a disk;
the lifetime of binary BHs is longer than the Hubble Time if they are not embedded in gas.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how binary black holes (BH) form and merge, which is important for the interpretation of gravitational wave observations of merging BHs by LISA and LIGO.
the evolution and merger of supermassive black hole binaries.
the formation and evolution of binary supermassive black hole systems, and their connection with the observed quasar population.

, while it is possible that the binary lifetime is shorter than a Hubble time, it is unlikely that this is due to a stellar dynamical process, but is instead due to a gas dynamical process.
the formation of binary BH systems is a natural outcome of the galaxy formation process.
the merger of binary supermassive black hole systems is a generic consequence of hierarchical galaxy merging.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
binary black hole mergers from planet-like migrations is a promising mechanism to explain the origin of quasars.
binary black holes (BBH) mergers in galactic nuclei can be driven by the accretion of gas in a disk surrounding the binary.
the binary lifetime is set by the gas supply, not by the dynamics of the stellar background.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the merger of a BH binary is likely to be a fast and efficient process, which may be responsible for the observed quasar activity in many galaxies.

, while stellar dynamical evolution is too slow, gas dynamics can drive binary BHs to merger in a few Myr, a time scale that is short compared to the Hubble time, but long compared to the dynamical time in galactic bulges.
, in the context of the galaxy merger paradigm, BH binaries are expected to be short-lived, with a lifetime comparable to that of a gas disk.
